From the given Zener diode circuit diagram:
* Input voltage, $V_i = 120\text{ V}$
* Series resistance, $R = 5\text{ k}\Omega = 5000\Omega$
* Zener breakdown voltage, $V_Z = 50\text{ V}$
* Load resistance, $R_L = 10\text{ k}\Omega = 10000\Omega$

**(iii) Find load current $I_L$:**
The load resistor $R_L$ is in parallel with the Zener diode, so the voltage across $R_L$ is equal to the Zener voltage $V_Z$.
$$I_L = \frac{V_Z}{R_L} = \frac{50\text{ V}}{10\text{ k}\Omega} = \frac{50}{10000} = 0.005\text{ A} = 5\text{ mA}$$

**(i) Current through series resistance $R$ ($I$):**
The voltage drop across the series resistor $R$ is $V_i - V_Z$.
$$I = \frac{V_i - V_Z}{R} = \frac{120\text{ V} - 50\text{ V}}{5\text{ k}\Omega} = \frac{70\text{ V}}{5000\Omega} = 0.014\text{ A} = 14\text{ mA}$$

**(ii) Find zener current $I_Z$:**
Applying Kirchhoff's Current Law at the node:
$$I = I_Z + I_L$$
$$I_Z = I - I_L = 14\text{ mA} - 5\text{ mA} = 9\text{ mA}$$
proTip: Always calculate load current first in Zener regulator problems since the load voltage is fixed by the Zener breakdown voltage.
